done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 2
Close still publishes worker-authored test names, including tests it did not run.
Raise: Not done. `proof_list` copies the worker's `Proof list:` paragraph unchanged and appends statuses beneath it. The worker brief still instructs the worker to supply pytest node IDs. The new end-to-end test confirms that a nonexistent `test_empty` remains in the published list with a `not run` annotation. Close therefore neither writes the proof list from its run nor ensures that the list names only tests that ran.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
The named proof test accepts the behavior the Done-when item forbids, so it cannot catch this regression.
Raise: Test. Its assertion requires an unrun test to remain in the published proof list. The other new command-level test likewise accepts named tests after a command that provides no individual test results. Neither tests Close generating a list solely from tests that ran.
